subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw define and support a runtime-neutral agent-core protocol for embedded/no-Node ports, or should projects like MimiClaw remain independent external ports without a core compatibility contract?
rationale: The evidence shows current OpenClaw is intentionally Node-hosted, and supporting no-Node devices would affect runtime ownership, plugin SDK boundaries, sessions, tool execution, providers, storage, and security policy beyond a narrow code repair.

options.title: Keep As Runtime-Portability RFC
options.body: Use this issue to design the smallest stable protocol, conformance tests, and ownership boundary before accepting embedded, WASM, C, or Rust implementation work.

options.title: Scope To Plugin SDK Work
options.body: Limit near-term work to JSON-RPC/plugin-harness APIs and document that full no-Node ports are external compatibility efforts.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: Decide that OpenClaw remains a Node-hosted TypeScript/Gateway product and that external projects such as MimiClaw do not receive a compatibility promise.

recommendation.title: Keep As Runtime-Portability RFC
recommendation.body: Use this issue to design the smallest stable protocol, conformance tests, and ownership boundary before accepting embedded, WASM, C, or Rust implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant current history and prior issue discussion are around agent runtime extraction, runtime docs, and platform direction.
